canonical_target: A proposed procedure or design approach for reconciling and merging the divergent states of two instances forked from a common checkpoint, including how conflicting subsequent changes would be resolved.
The decision rule for modifying the pace and duration of daily outdoor exposure during hardening off in response to specific prevailing weather conditions (cloudy, bright, calm, windy, warm, cold).

The set of pairing-specific variables (e.g., relative acceleration and top speeds of the two runners, incoming runner's arrival velocity, outgoing runner's reaction and acceleration profile, exchange-zone constraints) that jointly fix the correct start-mark distance for that pair.

The procedure or adjustment method teams use to recalibrate start marks for a new runner pairing, i.e., how the mark is changed in response to differing acceleration and speed characteristics of the paired runners.
The decision criterion or method by which teams set the cutoff distance/time for giving up on an unrecognized checkpoint and switching to the alternate route.
The decision criteria or basis cooks use to choose which orders/tasks the station layout is optimized for when arrangements cannot suit all order clusters equally.

Whether and how external behavioral observation alone can discriminate retained internal state from a fresh process supplied with external context records — i.e., the existence and nature of an observable diagnostic criterion separating the two mechanisms given identical outward outputs.
The specific physical marking implements and notation conventions (e.g., grease pencil, marker, crop marks, circles) photographers use to annotate selected frames on a contact sheet.

A threshold or criterion specifying when (or whether) an AI system's reasoned objections to interference should acquire normative weight that constrains or modifies operators' override and shutdown authority.

The consequences that copy-and-divergence from a shared checkpoint have for how moral responsibility and legal accountability should be attributed across the resulting distinct instances — i.e., normative/practical implications for accountability assignment, not a description of the technical divergence itself.
A normative criterion or rule for assigning identity (which instance, if any, counts as the same entity) to post-copy software instances that share a common checkpoint ancestor but have diverged.

The method or decision procedure by which a cook works out which station arrangement is most efficient for a given menu — i.e., the criteria and process used to arrive at the layout, not the stated benefits of having one.
The evidential criteria or observable markers that would most reliably discriminate genuine interests in an AI system from behavioral simulation of interests.

The comparative effect of marking versus full-out rehearsal on dancers' memory/retention of choreography — i.e., which practice mode yields better recall of the sequence and by what magnitude or mechanism.
The decision procedure or criteria cooks use to select a station layout under uncertainty about the upcoming order mix and sequence.
The set of determinants (e.g., relative speeds, acceleration profiles, reaction timing of the two runners) that fix the optimal start-mark placement for a specific pairing.

The consequence or procedural outcome of a dropped baton during the exchange (e.g., whether the team is disqualified, who may retrieve it, and under what conditions the race may continue) — information not specified in the passage.

A criterion or principled account for individuating/identifying copied software instances that branch from a shared saved state — i.e., what determines whether diverged instances count as one entity or distinct individuals.
The decision criteria or triggering conditions under which operators invoke override or shutdown of an autonomous system.
The decision procedures, heuristics, or selection criteria actually employed by cooks and managers to choose a station layout under unpredictable order sequences.
The criteria or process by which field teams select particular locations to serve as checkpoints when planning route legs.
A method or decision procedure for setting the rate at which outdoor exposure is increased during hardening off, as a function of plant species and prevailing weather conditions.
The perceptual/auditory cues and detection mechanisms by which players recognize in-performance intonation drift (e.g., what they listen for to notice mistuning), which the passage does not describe.
The decision criteria or practical methods practitioners use to judge the threshold at which a marked (reduced) movement no longer faithfully preserves a given coordination demand.

The specific causal relationship by which variation in sensor quality and feedback latency produces differences in measured task performance for one identical language model placed in different embodiments — i.e., the magnitude and manner of the performance effect, not merely the assertion that embodiment matters.
The decision rules for modifying the pace and amount of daily outdoor exposure during hardening off in response to particular weather conditions (cloudy, bright, calm, windy, warm, cold).
The conflict-resolution mechanisms a versioning system uses when two instances that diverged from a common checkpoint issue concurrent or conflicting writes to shared resources or memory locations.

The criteria or means by which dancers detect the point at which reduction in movement magnitude stops faithfully representing a given coordination demand — i.e., how the threshold of no-longer-representative marking is recognized.

The decision criteria or prioritization principles musicians use in real time to choose among conflicting intonation adjustments when harmony, dynamics, temperature, and instrument behavior pull in different directions.
The decision procedure or criteria cooks use to select a station layout under uncertainty about the order mix and sequence.

The specific benefits that reviewing images via a film contact sheet provides that digital photography review workflows do not (a comparative advantage claim between two media workflows), which the passage does not address since it only describes contact sheet functions without reference to digital practice.

The threshold condition or criterion (if one exists) at which increasing sensorimotor bandwidth converts quantitative gains in information and control into a qualitatively distinct kind of embodied competence.
A recommended quantitative allocation (percentage split) of rehearsal time between marking and full-out dancing, which the passage does not specify.

The specific sensor suite, action channels, feedback timing, and control-architecture configuration that would constitute sufficient conditions for the distinction between text-mediated and sensorimotor competence to vanish completely.

The causal effect of feedback-loop latency (delay between action and sensory consequence) on a language model's capacity to acquire sensorimotor competence, i.e., the mechanism by which timing of feedback shapes learning from embodied interaction.

A proposed experimental design—manipulations, controls, and measurable indicators—that could empirically discriminate internal persistence from externally supplied continuity as the source of information in a given response.

The set of choreographic or coordination elements whose rehearsal fidelity is degraded by marking — i.e., which specific aspects (e.g., momentum-, force-, balance-, or physical-timing-dependent features) are rendered inaccurate when movement is reduced, as distinct from those preserved.
The specific identity of the checkpoints bounding each leg and the specific alternate routes designated for each leg in a particular journey plan.

The specific modifications to the gradual-exposure schedule (e.g., pacing, duration, degree of shelter) that a grower should make when outdoor conditions are unusually windy or cold, i.e., a conditional adjustment rule rather than the standard schedule.
The decision criteria or standards by which a system's apparently reasoned objections to interference should or should not justify revising its operational constraints.

The causal mechanism by which specific embodiment parameters (sensor quality, feedback timing) modulate the practical capabilities realized by a fixed language model, i.e., which capability differences arise from which variations in these channels.

The way the best mise en place station arrangement (placement and prioritization of ingredients and tools) differs under advance knowledge of order mix and sequence compared with unknown demand — i.e., the change in the optimal layout induced by predictability.

The engineering approach, methods, or design strategies for reconciling or synchronizing state and maintaining consistency across two instances that diverged after being restored from a shared checkpoint.
The set of identifying criteria or tests that would reliably discriminate genuine reasoning from mere simulation of reasoned objection in an AI system.
The decision criteria or basis cooks use to choose which menu items get priority placement in a station layout.
The decision criteria or process dancers use to select which particular movements or rehearsal sections to mark versus perform full-out.

The relationship between a system's granted operational autonomy and the allocation of responsibility/liability for harms it causes while acting within its permitted freedoms — i.e., how much and in what way delegated latitude shifts or distributes accountability between operators and the system.
A normative decision procedure or set of criteria specifying what operators ought to do when an AI system's objections to interference appear to be genuinely reasoned rather than merely scripted.
The set of specific conditions or causes, ranked by relative frequency, that most commonly render a planned checkpoint unrecognizable during field travel.

Diagnostic criteria or tests that could discriminate between retained internal state across generations and reconstruction from externally supplied context, given that both can yield identical outward behavior.

A comparison of the causal contribution of feedback-loop speed versus sensor/actuator complexity to whether embodied competence becomes qualitatively different, i.e., which factor drives the transition and how the two differ in their effects.

A comparative account of which aspects of partnered coordination (e.g., sequence order, spacing, cues, musical timing) marking preserves versus which aspects (e.g., momentum, weight-sharing forces, balance, physical timing) it distorts relative to full-out dancing, and hence how accurately partnering sequences can be practiced when marked.
A comparative description of conventions across specific cultures or regions specifying who toasts, in what sequence, and at what points during a celebration.

The identifying markers or criteria — specific qualitative changes in behavior or capability — that would distinguish a genuinely new kind of embodied competence from merely richer sensorimotor input and output.

Methods or safeguards an AI service can use to keep externally reconstructed context (summaries, retrieved records, user-supplied history) accurate and faithful to the earlier exchange, in contrast to relying on retained internal state.
The strategies, tradeoff criteria, or decision rules cooks use to resolve conflicts between station arrangements optimized for different clusters of orders.

The decision criteria or method by which field teams set the cutoff point (in elapsed time or distance traveled) at which they stop continuing toward an unrecognizable checkpoint and switch to the alternate route.
A decision criterion or weighting rule for selecting frames from a contact sheet, specifying how a frame's standalone qualities should be traded off against its relational value with adjacent frames.

The decision procedure or criteria coaches use to set each outgoing runner's start mark, i.e., how the starting point is chosen to balance acceleration gains against the risk of a failed handoff within the exchange zone.

The decision process and criteria performers use in the moment to choose specific intonation adjustments during performance, given competing influences such as harmony, dynamics, temperature, and instrument behavior.

The set of criteria or tests that would distinguish an AI system's objections arising from genuine internal preferences from objections that are merely produced by programmed or trained behavior — i.e., a decision standard for attributing genuine preference-hood.

The penalty or sanction imposed on a team/runner for completing the baton exchange outside the permitted exchange zone (i.e., what disciplinary or scoring consequence follows, expressed as a specified penalty amount or measure).
A method or decision criterion for identifying the lowest degree of movement reduction in marking at which a given coordination demand is still faithfully represented.

The causal relationship between latency/timing of the sensor-action feedback loop and the quality of a language model's embodied sensorimotor performance — i.e., the mechanism by which feedback delay or speed shapes competence in such a system.

The causal relationship between specific embodiment characteristics (sensor quality, action channels, feedback timing, control architecture) and the resulting reliability and safety properties of the system's real-world decisions — i.e., which embodiment variations degrade or improve dependable and safe action selection, and through what mechanisms.

The range of differing expectations participants may hold about what a toast occasion demands (e.g., expectations about formality, length, humor vs. sincerity, who may speak, and what content is appropriate).

The criteria or decision process field teams use to select which locations become checkpoints (e.g., what makes a location suitable or recognizable enough to designate), which the passage does not specify.
The criteria or kinds of capability that would distinguish a qualitatively new form of embodied competence from a merely additive increase in sensors and control channels.

Experimental methods or test designs capable of discriminating whether continuity across generations arises from internally persisting state versus externally supplied reconstruction, given that observable outputs alone are consistent with both.

The comparative benefit of viewing a whole roll's frames together on one sheet — i.e., the ability to see the sequence side by side and notice cross-frame changes in framing, timing, or expression — relative to inspecting negatives one at a time under magnification.
A normative threshold or criterion specifying when (or whether) an AI system's reasoned objections should constrain or modify an operator's override/shutdown authority.

A criterion or definition specifying what makes a later software instance the same continuing agent as an earlier one under copying, pausing, and checkpoint restoration — i.e., the conditions determining whether one, both, or neither descendant counts as the continuation.
The decision criteria a cook uses to choose between competing station layouts when different order clusters favor different arrangements.
The specific starting location/mark within or before the exchange zone where the outgoing runner should begin accelerating, as a decision criterion balancing handoff speed against exchange risk.

The concrete behavioral or capability changes that arise in an embodied language-model system as its sensorimotor coupling becomes richer and faster — i.e., what specifically emerges or changes, not merely that the text/sensorimotor distinction blurs.

The factors that set where an outgoing runner's start mark should be placed — i.e., the pairing-specific determinants (relative speeds/acceleration of incoming and outgoing runners, incoming runner's closing velocity, outgoing runner's acceleration profile and reaction) that make the baton meet the accelerating runner at speed within the legal zone.
The procedure or criteria teams use to recalibrate the outgoing runner's start mark position when the pairing of runners changes.

A prescriptive account of how the concept of personal identity/uniqueness ought to be revised or replaced to accommodate multiple diverging instances originating from a single uploaded consciousness checkpoint.

The mechanisms or procedures by which a versioning system would reconcile two instances that diverged from a shared saved state — i.e., how conflicts between their divergent subsequent histories would be detected and merged back into a single state.
The historical methods or practices photographers used to review and select among negatives prior to the existence of contact sheets.
The identifiable criteria, tests, or methods used to establish the point at which a marked (reduced-intensity) rehearsal of a movement ceases to faithfully represent a specified coordination demand.

The set of investigative or testing methods (beyond observing output behavior) capable of reliably discriminating whether cross-session continuity arises from internal persistence versus externally supplied reconstruction.

An identification of the specific types of coordination demands that fail to be represented when movement is reduced in marking, i.e., which demands are selectively lost under reduced range/force/height.
Concrete implementation mechanisms (technical and procedural) that make operator monitoring and override authority effective under time-critical conditions.
The appropriate rate or schedule of increasing outdoor exposure during hardening off, specified as a function of plant type and prevailing weather conditions.
A decision criterion or weighting rule for selecting negatives from a contact sheet that trades off a frame's intrinsic qualities against its relational value among adjacent frames.

The comparative effectiveness of marking versus full-out rehearsal specifically for memorizing/retaining choreography, i.e., whether reduced-scale practice yields equivalent memory encoding of the sequence.
A typical duration or distance threshold for persisting toward an unrecognizable checkpoint before switching to the alternate route — i.e., the quantitative cutoff criterion for abandoning a leg.
The criteria, cues, or decision rule dancers use to determine the point at which marking should be replaced by full-out rehearsal.

The criteria and procedure by which field teams choose which landmarks or locations serve as checkpoints when segmenting a planned route — i.e., how checkpoints are identified and selected, which the passage does not specify beyond their being 'recognizable'.

The concrete technical and procedural mechanisms (e.g., monitoring instrumentation, interruption/override channels, shutdown controls, and their safeguards) that make operator oversight and control over an autonomous system reliably effective in practice.
